bull_bear.body: Debt-funded capex (₹160-165Cr net debt); focus on utilization optimization before new capex; dividend policy not disclosed; reinvestment prioritized over buybacks or dividends
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity price volatility (steel, energy) with 1-2 quarter lag; geopolitical disruption in shipping routes (Middle East); ramp-up delays in new capacity; labor training and operational synchronization; legal dispute with MSCB over solar banking policy
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but confident in FY27 margin recovery; emphasizes operational discipline, pricing power, and long-term capacity needs; management is proactive on customer diversification and cost control
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 12 new product developments in FY26 (including for Vestas, L&T) significantly increase complexity but also revenue potential; machining utilization at 50% already despite only 30-40% product development complete — indicates faster-than-expected learning curve; INR depreciation vs Yuan (20%) is a bigger competitive advantage than vs USD (10%)
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet as at 30.06.26 (Rs Crore, unaudited): Net Worth 100.98, Long Term Borrowings 162.75, Short Term Borrowings 79.93, against Total Assets of 466.53 — borrowings exceed net worth on the deck's own figures.
- Non-Current Assets of 297.22 Rs Crore as at 30.06.26 (299.76 as at 31.03.26) reflect the capital already sunk into the 45,000 TPA build.
- The deck states no dividend, buyback or payout policy, and does not disclose how the proposed greenfield expansion to over 100,000 MT would be funded.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Long-term supply partnerships with six of the top 15 global wind OEMs (Vestas, Vayona/erstwhile Siemens Gamesa, GE, Nordex, Adani, Envision) plus Indian OEM Senvion
- Long-term contracts with major wind gearbox manufacturers Flender Drives and ZF Wind, diversifying beyond pure wind-turbine castings
- Tier-1 supplier relationships across industrial machinery, mining, plastic injection and pumps (Terex, Milacron, Wilo), giving facility versatility to redeploy capacity beyond wind with reasonable lead time
- Zero TRIR (safety incident rate) maintained for four consecutive years, supported by ISO 45001 certification
- 98% sand recycling through thermal and mechanical reclamation, reducing virgin raw material consumption and cost
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Heavy sector concentration in wind energy — The wind sector accounted for over 80% of revenues; management's own mitigation is that facilities are versatile enough to serve other large-casting applications with reasonable lead time, implying the concentration itself is structural.
- Customer/OEM concentration — Demand is concentrated among a handful of global wind OEMs (Vestas, Vayona/erstwhile Siemens Gamesa, GE, Nordex, Adani, Envision) and gearbox makers (Flender Drives, ZF Wind); the Company is actively adding customers (Senvion, GE India, Adani; onboarding Nordex and Envision) specifically to mitigate this concentration risk.
- Commodity price volatility in key raw materials — Input prices for pig iron and CRCA scrap are volatile and were further pressured by the West Asia conflict; the Company hedges via quarterly customer contracts, but there can be a one-quarter lag in passing on price changes, exposing near-term margins.
- Foreign-exchange exposure on export earnings — With exports at roughly 25-30% of revenue, currency movements are a structural risk; mitigated via Foreign Currency Term Loans and currency swap arrangements to create a natural hedge.
- Skilled manpower availability — Availability of skilled labour, particularly for critical operations such as fettling, remains a challenge; the Company is pursuing automation to reduce dependence on manual processes.
- Rising financial leverage from the capex programme — The ₹217 crore capex programme was funded partly through debt; the Debt-Equity Ratio rose to 2.25 (from 1.45) and Interest Coverage Ratio fell to 2.37 (from 3.42), reflecting borrowings availed for the capital expenditure.
- Execution/ramp-up risk on newly commissioned capacity — FY26 profitability was already dented by higher outsourcing and operating costs, manpower/overhead costs, and discounted export pricing during the development phase of the in-house machining facility; expected margin benefits depend on successful utilisation ramp-up of the new foundry, machining and solar capacity through FY27.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Wind domestic: Primary revenue driver; OEM exports: 25-30% of revenue; Direct exports: Stable; Gearbox: Growing segment; Non-wind: New customers added (Mahindra, L&T, Terex, Millikron, Willow)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- "Working with 6 out of 15 Leading Wind OEMs", with customers shown split between wind and non-wind and a named customer described as "(erstwhile Siemens Gamesa)".
- SWOT strengths cited: "Ability to Produce large castings up to 30 MT", "Established products with Top Global OEMs" and "Ability to build large capacities with capital efficiency".
- Entry-barrier framing: "Excellent growth opportunities in Renewable's with high entry barriers", plus "India is being converted as manufacturing Hub offers growing casting demand", "Trade wars/Global Sentiments favor India's demand" and "INR depreciation against USD and CNY, favouring Indian foundries".
- Acknowledged constraints: "Limited Capacity compared to peers (scaled up to 45,000 TPA, planning to expand further)" and "Dependency on outsourced machining (~20,000 TPA in-house machining established)".
- Part of the Shirgaokar Brothers Group (Since 1913), whose businesses are listed as Sugar, Foundry, General Engineering, IT & Hospitality with a group annual turnover of Rs 2,700 Crores — a group figure, not the listed entity's.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Guidance] "FY 27 is expected to have a ~33% revenue growth over FY 26", with the revenue-streams chart showing FY 26-27 P of 500 Rs Cr versus 376 Rs Cr in FY 25-26, "Based on executable Order Book Projection" — management flags this projection "may be subject to change based on market conditions".
- [Guidance] "Despite moderation in Q1, FY27 PBDIT margin is expected to improve by >300 bps, driven by higher volumes, increased export contribution and growing contributions from in-house machining."
- [Industry - wind] "India's installed wind capacity to more than double from 51 GW in 2026 to 107 GW by 2030" and "Global cumulative capacity projected to exceed 2 TW by 2030, driven by record-breaking annual installations" (source: GEWC Global Wind Report 2026).
- [Industry - castings] 2024 casting market of 110 Mn MT total, "Global: $ 160 bn" and "India: $ 13.2 bn"; large casting demand split "Wind : 1.5 Mn MT" and "Non-Wind: ~6 Mn MT" (sources: Indian Institute of Foundrymen, Foundry Planet).
- [Exceptional item] The income statement records exceptional items described as "statutory provision for new labour code" — 0.01 Rs Crore for the quarter ended 31.03.26 and 0.65 Rs Crore for the year ended 31.03.26.

It serves both domestic and international customers, with long-term supply partnerships built over the years with several of the top global wind OEMs.

outlook.body: revenue growth: 33% to ₹500Cr; margin: +300+ bps to ~16.1%; order inflow: Strong, with new customers (Mahindra, L&T) and Vestas contract pending; capex/commissioning: No new capex announced, land acquisition targeted for FY27 to support next expansion
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: ₹500-530Cr visibility, with confirmed orders from Vestas, Siemens Gamesa (Viona), Nordex, GE, Envision, Adani, Flender, ZF, Mahindra, L&T
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Next capacity expansion (beyond 45K MT) contingent on land acquisition in FY27; potential to reach ₹780Cr+ revenue with full product mix utilization; solar captive power (10MW) reduces energy cost volatility
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Stay ahead of evolving wind industry requirements as the sector transitions to larger turbine platforms, through continuous investment in capacity, technology and capabilities
- Build long-term partnerships with leading global wind OEMs by delivering quality, reliability and engineering excellence
- Diversify beyond core wind-OEM castings into gearbox manufacturers (Flender Drives, ZF Wind) and industrial Tier-1 customers (mining, plastic injection, pumps) to reduce sector concentration
- Expand customer portfolio to mitigate concentration risk - added Senvion India, GE India and Adani, with Nordex and Envision being onboarded
- Embed sustainability into manufacturing via captive solar power, energy-efficient processes and resource optimisation
- Undertake automation initiatives to reduce dependence on manual/skilled labour, particularly in fettling operations
- Diversify and secure alternative sources for critical raw materials such as pig iron and CRCA scrap
- Maintain a natural hedge against foreign-exchange risk via Foreign Currency Term Loans and currency swap arrangements
- No equity dividend evidenced in this bundle; the Board recommended a dividend only on the 10% Redeemable Cumulative Preference Shares for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM. Shareholders were also asked to approve raising the Company's overall borrowing limit from Rs.200 crore to Rs.250 crore, indicating continued reliance on debt to fund growth/capex alongside internal accruals.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 was a transformational capex year for SGIL, marked by completion of a brownfield foundry expansion (foundry capacity raised from 30,000 TPA to 45,000 TPA, with a new production line and single-product weight capability raised from 23 MT to 30 MT), establishment of a new fettling and inspection facility sized for the enlarged 45,000 TPA capacity (with activities relocated from existing facilities), commissioning of new in-house machining and surface-treatment facilities with 20,000 TPA installed capacity (including new machining/coating processes and customer approvals for the facilities), and expansion of captive solar power capacity from 2 MW to 10 MW. The programme was executed over roughly 12-18 months and funded through the Rights Issue completed in October 2024, internal accruals and debt financing. In parallel, the Company developed 12 new products across major OEM customers for turbines up to 5 MW, to utilise the enhanced capacity. Management expects the benefits of ramping these newly commissioned facilities to progressively reflect in financial performance from FY 2026-27 onward.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global and Indian wind energy markets remain on a strong growth trajectory, with the West Asia conflict further accelerating renewable-energy installations
- India's emergence as a manufacturing hub for multinational OEMs is unlocking significant global demand for domestic casting manufacturers
- Depreciation of the Indian Rupee, particularly against the Chinese Yuan, is improving the competitiveness of Indian castings in global markets
- Geopolitical shifts, including regional tensions and trade wars, are increasing sourcing from India and strengthening export opportunities for Indian foundries
- New customer additions and product developments are broadening the Company's addressable market, backed by enhanced production capacity
- Ramp-up of the newly commissioned 20,000 TPA in-house machining facility and 10 MW captive solar plant is expected to drive margin expansion and cost optimisation from FY27 onward
- Company remains heavily dependent on the wind sector (over 80% of revenues), though facilities are versatile enough to serve other large-casting applications with reasonable lead time
- West Asia conflict is pressuring input raw-material prices; commodity costs are hedged via quarterly customer contracts, though there can be a one-quarter lag in passing on price changes
- FY26 revenue growth was muted due to project activities/operational disruption from the brownfield expansion, slower offtake from newly acquired Wind Domestic OEM customers, and lower OEM Export revenue during the product transition to higher-MW turbine platforms; Gearbox and Non-Wind segments partly offset this
- Executable order book for FY 2026-27 is projected to grow by over 33% compared to the previous year, surpassing the ₹500 crore mark
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Synergy Green expanded foundry and machining capacity to 45K and 20K MT/year, enabling 5MW turbine production and driving 33% FY27 revenue guidance to ₹500Cr, but FY26 margins were pressured by transition costs and commodity inflation; margin expansion of 300+ bps is expected in FY27 as utilization ramps and pricing pass-throughs catch up.

open.item: Company expects to deliver healthy double-digit revenue growth in FY 2026-27, backed by new customer additions, product developments and enhanced production capacity.
Executable order book for FY 2026-27 is projected to grow by over 33% compared to the previous year, surpassing the ₹500 crore mark.
EBITDA margins are expected to expand by over 300 basis points YoY in FY 2026-27 on the back of the machining facility and captive solar plant ramp-up and economies of scale.

West Asia conflict is pressuring input raw-material prices; while key commodities are hedged through customer contracts, there could be a one-quarter lag in passing on input-price changes to customers.
Targeting 50% green production by 2030 as part of renewable energy and carbon reduction initiatives.
Export revenues, which contributed approximately 27% of revenue in FY 2025-26, are expected to remain stable in the 25%-30% range going forward.
Company is onboarding Nordex and Envision as new customers, in addition to already-added Senvion India, GE India and Adani, to mitigate customer concentration risk.
